decisions.title: Direct Codex requests and manual editing share drill files
decisions.context: The user wants to dictate coaching goals directly in Codex and also create or edit drills manually in Training Ground. A form must not become a required middle step.
decisions.decision: Support both paths over the same JSON drill files. Describe a drill explains direct Codex requests and offers a board action, followed by an optional expandable written-brief helper. Dictation happens in Codex itself. Do not add paid AI or speech API integrations unless the user explicitly asks later.
decisions.consequences: The coach can move between agent-authored and manual changes. The watcher refreshes file changes; conflicts protect unsaved edits. The optional helper only prepares text and retains a browser draft when available. It neither sends a model request nor records speech.

decisions.title: Bookmarks and brief drafts stay separate from drill files
decisions.context: The library refresh adds saved-drill shortcuts and a reusable coaching-brief draft. These are browsing conveniences rather than changes to a drill's coaching content.
decisions.decision: Store saved-drill IDs and brief fields in optional browser localStorage. Keep workspace navigation and coaching-panel selection in local React state. Continue storing all drill content in drills/*.json through the existing persistence layer.
decisions.consequences: No schema or server storage change is required. Bookmarks and drafts are specific to the browser and can be lost if its storage is cleared. If storage is unavailable, the current form and bookmarks still work for the visit.

decisions.title: One render path: every pixel comes from BoardSvg
decisions.context: The editor shows a drill on screen; PNG, MP4 and GIF exports must show the same drill. Two drawing implementations (screen + export) inevitably drift.
decisions.decision: BoardSvg is a pure function of a BoardSnapshot. The editor mounts it live; exports call renderToStaticMarkup on the same component and rasterize the SVG string to a canvas. There is no second draw path anywhere.
decisions.consequences: Exports are pixel-identical to the editor by construction. The cost is a constraint: BoardSvg must stay free of foreignObject, webfonts and external hrefs (they break SVG-to-canvas rasterization), and editor-only chrome (handles, previews) lives in an overlay passed as children.

decisions.title: Drills are JSON files, not SQLite rows
decisions.context: Evaluated during the 2026-06-12 enhancement pass at Kyle's request: would a SQLite database add value? Candidates considered: drill storage, a library search index, practice-session logs, roster history.
decisions.decision: No SQLite. drills/*.json stays the source of truth and no database is wired in. The file layout IS the product's agent route: Claude/Codex author drill files directly on a subscription (no API costs), chokidar pushes SSE so files appear in the library in about a second, git gives history/diff/backup, and a coach can eyeball or hand-edit any drill. A binary store would subtract every one of those properties and add a native dependency (better-sqlite3 compiles against the Node ABI) to gain indexes and transactions that a personal library measured in tens of files cannot feel. In-memory search over library summaries is already instant at this scale.
decisions.consequences: Search, tags and previews compute from files on demand. Revisit only if a concrete feature needs what files can't give: full-text search across many hundreds of drills, concurrent multi-writer sessions, or per-rep analytics. If that day comes, SQLite should arrive as a rebuildable INDEX over the files (cache, not truth) so the agent route survives.

decisions.title: SVG board instead of a canvas library
decisions.context: Tactics boards need crisp lines at any zoom, easy hit-testing for drag/select, and text labels. Konva/canvas engines offer scene graphs but rasterize, and would have forced the export pipeline to share their draw code.
decisions.decision: Hand-rolled SVG components with raw pointer events and setPointerCapture. 1 SVG user unit = 1 meter, so geometry is the data model.
decisions.consequences: Free DOM hit-testing, crisp markings, declarative React rendering, and renderToStaticMarkup gives exports for free. Scale ceiling (~hundreds of nodes) is far above a soccer drill's needs.

decisions.title: Save dense, load sparse
decisions.context: Sparse steps (only movers listed, forward-fill for the rest) are pleasant to hand-write and review; dense steps (every entity every step) are independently readable and make scrubbing trivially correct.
decisions.decision: Both: files may be sparse (agents are encouraged to write them that way), the resolver forward-fills at load, and the app serializes dense on save with via/ease kept only on the step where they were explicit.
decisions.consequences: Agent files stay reviewable; app-saved files are bigger but every step stands alone. The serializer must strip transition fields from forward-filled copies (covered by tests).

decisions.title: One drag = one undo entry (zundo pause/rewind/replay)
decisions.context: A drag emits dozens of store updates; naive history makes undo useless. zundo records the pre-set state on every tracked change, so simply pausing during the drag and resuming at the end records the wrong base state.
decisions.decision: beginGesture pauses history and stashes the pre-drag drill; endGesture rewinds to the stash while paused, resumes, then replays the final state as a single tracked change.
decisions.consequences: Ctrl+Z after a drag returns exactly to the pre-drag pose. Anything that moves entities continuously (drags, arrow endpoints, zone resize) must run inside a gesture.

decisions.title: MP4 via WebCodecs + mediabunny, rendered offline
decisions.context: mp4-muxer and webm-muxer are deprecated in favor of mediabunny (same author). Realtime captureStream recording drops frames and can't control quality; ffmpeg is not installed and shouldn't be required.
decisions.decision: Exports render frames offline at a fixed timestep (deterministic), encode through WebCodecs hardware H.264 when the OS provides it, and fall back to VP9/WebM. mediabunny muxes both containers.
decisions.consequences: Pixel-exact, faster-than-realtime exports with zero system dependencies; Chromium-only (acceptable: local app, Chrome/Edge documented). Windows N editions without codecs degrade to WebM automatically.

decisions.title: Narration records the live board via Region Capture
decisions.context: A narrated take needs the coach's voice synced to whatever they do live (play, scrub, point). That is inherently realtime, unlike the offline render exports.
decisions.decision: getDisplayMedia tab capture cropped to the board element via CropTarget, mixed with the mic, recorded by MediaRecorder (MP4 when supported, else WebM) in 1s timeslices.
decisions.consequences: The one capture path that is NOT BoardSvg-rasterized — it records the actual screen, cursor included (a feature for pointing). Chromium-only; browser Stop-sharing ends the take cleanly.

decisions.title: Zoom/pan is a CSS transform around the board, not SVG viewBox math
decisions.context: Wheel-zoom and panning must not disturb the pure renderer or the export pipeline, and pointer math has to stay correct while zoomed.
decisions.decision: BoardViewport wraps the board in a CSS-transformed div. getScreenCTM() folds ancestor CSS transforms into the screen-to-board conversion, so every existing drag/draw interaction works unmodified, and exports (which mount their own BoardSvg) never see the transform.
decisions.consequences: Zero changes to BoardSvg or interactions; view state is presentation-only (not in the store, not persisted, resets per drill).

decisions.title: Rosters and settings never enter the public repo
decisions.context: The repo is public and the roster holds children's names. data/settings.json churns with per-machine state.
decisions.decision: data/rosters.json and data/settings.json are gitignored; the server serves defaults when they're missing. Drill files remain committed (they are the shareable content) with a README warning to prefer first names, initials or numbers when stamping roster identities into drills meant for pushing.
decisions.consequences: Kids' names stay on the coach's machine by default. A fresh clone starts with an empty roster.

decisions.title: The server stays a dumb file layer
decisions.context: Validation, resolution and rendering all live in the app/model layer; agents also bypass the server entirely by writing files.
decisions.decision: Express does file CRUD with atomic tmp+rename writes, rev stamping for conflict detection, delete-to-trash, SSE change push, and export blob writes. No validation, no business logic, plain .mjs with no build step.
decisions.consequences: Two clients (app via HTTP, agents via the filesystem) stay equal citizens; the server never disagrees with the app about what a valid drill is because it has no opinion.

decisions.title: Playback clock survives hidden tabs
decisions.context: Browsers freeze requestAnimationFrame in hidden tabs; a coach who tabs away mid-playback would return to a frozen animation, and headless verification environments see the same freeze.
decisions.decision: The playback clock advances via rAF for smooth visible frames plus a 100ms watchdog interval computing real elapsed time, so time keeps flowing (coarsely) when the tab is hidden.
decisions.consequences: Animations finish wherever the tab is; scrub state is always time-true rather than frame-count-true.
